description: Exactly what the shell's own page needs, and nothing more. That page is the app's first-run and diagnostics surface (`dist/index.html`) — the only document that runs on the shell's own origin — and its entire JavaScript surface is the app's own commands (`invoke`) and the subscription to the sidecar's `sidecar://event` stream (`listen`). So this capability grants two things: `default`, the app's own permission set (the commands in `src/commands.rs`, listed in `permissions/default.toml`), and the two event permissions the subscription needs — the listen, and the unlisten that `listen` hands back. What the shell does *not* do from JavaScript is gone: the process plugin (the page never restarts or exits the app through it — the native menu does that in Rust), the opener, dialog, os and fs plugins (the page opens no URL, picks no file and reads no file; the shell's own commands do all of that in Rust), and the `core:` collectors — `core:default` expands to the image, menu, tray, path and resources plugins (`plugin:image|from_path` is a bare `std::fs::read` with no scope check, and a forged menu id reaches `src-tauri/src/shell.rs`) and to the window and app commands no document ever calls: the window title, the theme, the zoom and the decorations are the shell's own app commands (`set_window_title`, `set_theme`, `set_zoom`, `set_decorations`), which run in Rust, where the ACL does not gate them. Declaring the app manifest in `build.rs` switched the ACL on for local origins too, so this replaced their former implicit access — and it is the capability a hardened build keeps, dropping the deliberately broad `desktop-everything`. The store plugin is deliberately **not** granted: `tauri-plugin-store` does no scope check of its own (`store|load` takes any path, absolute or not), and the store it keeps (`preferences.json`) holds the unredacted database connection string. The shell reaches the store through Rust (`state::set_pref`), which the ACL does not gate, so the permission would expose the password and buy nothing.
